content.text: A short summary of the theory around the power of a point with respect to a circle and around radical axes, together with a collection of my favorite problems. In difficulty the problems are mostly around the level of IMO problems, so the collection is not entirely suitable for complete beginners in this topic.
Throughout this handout, by the term
we will also mean a circle of
; points will therefore be circles as well, and it will be very useful to view them this way. A tangent to such a point circle is any line that passes through it.
The power of a point with respect to a point is the square of their distance.
Points on the circle have power zero, points outside the circle have positive power and points inside the circle have negative power.
The definition above gives a useful criterion for whether two points are at the same distance from the center of such a circle:
